about: Four pairs of versicles, three of them taken from the psalms. The first two are one continuous passage: Psalm 84, verses 7 and 8, taken in order and split between two voices. The third is Psalm 101, verse 2. The fourth — Dóminus vobíscum — is not from a psalm and falls here for the first time in the Mass; the priest will say it again several times, always before something he is about to do together with the people.

s01.narrative: The priest stays bowed at the foot of the altar and goes on, alternating with the server. One word more is said at the foot — Orémus, aloud — and with it the priest goes up to the altar.

s02.translation: O God, Thou wilt turn and give us life.

s03.translation: And Thy people will rejoice in Thee.

s04.translation: Show us Thy mercy, O Lord.

s07.translation: And let my cry come unto Thee.

w003.function: A participle passive in form but reflexive in sense: not “turned” but “having turned thyself”. The Latin psalter took the usage over from the Greek.

w004.function: Future: a petition dressed as a statement — thou wilt do it.

w007.function: A Roman word for the commons as against the patricians; in Scripture simply the people of God.

w009.function: A future: the people's rejoicing answers the promised quickening — God's turning first, the joy in Him after.

w011.function: Ablative after “in” (w010) — not “toward thee” but “in thee”: the joy has its place in God, not merely its direction.

w013.function: Dative with “Osténde” (w012). The same form is ablative in the “a nobis” of the priest's next prayer.

w015.function: The accusative of the plea: mercy here is a thing to be shown, almost to be seen — the verse asks God to let it be looked upon.

w018.function: The adjective salutáre used as a noun: the thing that saves. Here the object of “da” (w020), and so accusative.

w019.function: Agrees with “salutáre” (w018) — neuter, because that is the gender of the noun.

w023.function: An intensified audíre: not “hear” but “hear favourably” — that is, grant.

w027.function: Nominative: the subject of the clause. In the psalms a clamor is the voice of prayer, not an uproar.

w030.function: Accusative after “ad” (w029) — motion toward someone; the same form stood above in the ablative after “in” (w010).

w031.function: A subjunctive of wish — a petition, not a statement.

w032.function: A sentence with no verb: the Latin supplies neither “is” nor “be”, and so both readings stay open in it.

w033.function: One word carrying two: the preposition cum written after the pronoun instead of before it. So it always is with the personal pronouns — mecum, tecum, nobíscum.

w036.function: The old reading refers thy spirit to the grace of ordination; Jungmann hears a Semitism for simply thee. Both readings stand.

w037.function: Agrees with “spíritu” (w036). Singular — they speak to one priest, where he spoke to many.
